reports.title: Clarks Hill Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing on the lake has been decent the last couple weeks. Work your presentation slowly and be prepared to move around the lake more as bass haven’t bunched up yet. Concentrating on areas with high amounts of baitfish with a slowed approach is the key for nice bass this time of year.
Crappie are also on the move with the cooler water this month. Expect crappie to gather at mid-depth brush piles and around submerged cover going back into creeks. Typically, creeks in the middle and upper area of the lake fish well for crappie this time of year.

reports.title: Lake Sinclair fishing report
reports.text: LAKE SINCLAIR IS DOWN 1.6 FEET, 70’S – Bass fishing is good. Top water baits continue to produce a few fish, including large bass.

reports.title: Lake Russell fishing report
reports.text:
McDuffie angler showing off a nice area bass.
LAKE RUSSELL IS DOWN 1.1 FEET, 60’S – Bass fishing is good. Spotted Bass are roaming up on the points and flats all during the day and retreating to deep water stump beds. Either way, these bass are being caught all day long. The shallow water bass can be easily caught with Wiggle Warts, Sub Warts, and Rapala Shad Raps. This week, the deeper water bite has been fair for some bigger bass.

reports.title: Lake Oconee fishing report
reports.text: LAKE OCONEE IS DOWN 1.5 FEET, 70’S – Bass fishing is good. Most of the coves and creeks have large schools of bait in them and that is the key to the bass.

reports.title: Lake Jackson fishing report
reports.text: LAKE JACKSON IS FULL, 70’S – Bass fishing is fair.

reports.title: Public Fishing Area Report fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth: The warmer fall has kept the bass in shallower than typical years. The first part of December, bass should be targeted in 6-10’ depth of water and moving deeper as temperatures cool throughout the month. Plastic worms, swim baits, and crank baits should work well. The trick this time of the year is determining what depth of water the bass prefer to be. Late fall sampling revealed fish in open water at 6-10’ and along steep drop offs and creek channels.

reports.title: News to Know: fishing report
reports.text: Catchable-sized bluegill were stocked at Paradise PFA, while largemouth bass and smaller bluegill were transferred to Dawson Fish Hatchery. The bass will be used to establish all-female populations at locations across Georgia for a study comparing growth among largemouth bass genetic strains.

reports.title: Lake Hartwell fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and Black Bass: (Courtesy of Cole Wilson, Spot Chaser Guide Service ) — Hybrids and bass are schooling up and eating across the lake in preparation for the upcoming lake turnover. Fish points and humps across the lake in 10 to 30 feet of water with a walking bait like the IMA Skimmer in chrome or the Chug Bug, or a chartreuse herring Fluke weightless on top. Watch for schooling fish; they will be easy to catch if you get a bait on them while they are schooling. When the topwater slows, bottom fishing with a Carolina rig or shaky head and a Senko dragged over these points and humps can catch fish, too. Pay attention to the water. If it is dirty, stinky, or smelly, that is a good sign…

reports.title: Lake Allatoona fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie: (Report courtesy of Red Rooster Baits )
Crappie fishing on Lake Allatoona is about to bust loose! The crappie are starting to move around with the lake level dropping and the water temps dipping into the mid to high 60s. We trolled this past week using our newest jig, the “ Hammer Curl ,” which is our take on the traditional curly tail crappie jig, and it did not disappoint! We landed several nice slab crappie with the Hammer Curl in a few different colors that we chose due to water clarity and daylight conditions. We were looking for roaming schools of crappie that were making their way from brush out into open water. The crappie were suspended anywhere from 4′ to 10′ in 8′ to 12′…
